> 為無為，事無事，味無味.

Chapter 62 gave the place: sit, and you are there. Chapter 63 gives the daily work — how to sit in that corner while doing small things.

## 味 and 未 explain each other

味: 滋味也, from 口 and 未.

And 說文 defines 未 as 味也 — the two characters define each other. That reciprocal definition is usually a sign that the concept behind them is one thing seen from two sides.

未 also means 木重枝葉 — a tree at its heaviest with leaves, the time when the fruit has not yet ripened.

So 味無味 is: taste the taste of the not-yet-ripe.

Not "find flavor in blandness." Taste the thing at the stage before its flavor has formed — which is the only stage at which you can still work with it.

## 圖 is to draw the difficulty first

圖: 畫計難也 — to draw out the difficulty, then plan.

So 圖難於其易 is not "solve the hard thing while it is easy." It is: while it is still easy, draw the difficulty. Make the hard part visible before it exists.

That is a different instruction, and a much more useful one. Most difficulty is not solved early; it is simply not drawn early, and then arrives unannounced.

## 為大於其細

Do the great at its fine stage.

細 is the small, the fine, the thread. 天下大事，必作於細 — the great thing always starts in the fine thread.

作 is to rise, to come up. Not "is made from small parts": it rises out of them, and the small parts are where it is still shapeable.

## 大小多少，報怨以德

Treat the large as large and the many as many — and repay resentment with 德.

The first four characters are compressed: 大小多少 means to handle magnitude and quantity as they actually are. The clause that follows is the hardest instruction in the book, and it is placed casually.

報怨以德 is not permissiveness. 德 here is the same 德 as 玄德: the operating capacity that does not keep accounts. Two ledgers cannot both be maintained; if you keep the account of resentment, the account of capacity is not running.

## 聖人終不為大，故能成其大

He never treats anything as 大, and therefore can complete the 大.

The mechanism is the one from chapter 34: a thing that does not claim greatness does not have to defend a position, and what does not defend a position can grow.

## 輕諾必寡信，多易必多難

Light promises make for scant trust; many things taken as easy make for many difficulties.

易 appears three times in the chapter, and its fate is instructive: 圖難於其易 uses 易 as the early stage — genuinely the right time to work. 多易 uses 易 as the assumption that something is simple — and assumption converts the early stage into a later difficulty.

Same character, opposite outcomes, decided by whether the ease was observed or presumed.

## 聖人猶難之，故終無難矣

He still treats things as difficult, and therefore in the end there is no difficulty.

猶 — still, nevertheless. He does not stop treating things as hard; he stops treating them as hard after they have become hard.

## The shape of the chapter

Three 無's at the top (為無為，事無事，味無味) are the posture. The rest is timing: draw the difficulty early, work the fine thread, don't presume ease.

It is the most operational chapter in the book, and the only one that gives a working method rather than a condition.

## A test

Take one thing you are currently putting off because it is hard. Ask what it looked like two months ago, when it was fine and undrawn. If you can name that moment, the chapter's method becomes available next time.
